intro.title: Incident Response Training
intro.description: Even the best of us make mistakes. What matters is how quickly and effectively you respond. Practice the critical steps for different scenarios.

labels.criticalStepsCount: {count, plural, one {# critical step} other {# critical steps}}

why.title: Why This Matters
why.description: The FBI reports that quick action can help recover funds in Business Email Compromise cases. The difference between a minor incident and a major breach often comes down to how fast you report and respond. Practice these steps so they become second nature.

prompt.title: What should you do next?
prompt.subtitle: Select all the steps you would take to respond to this incident. Critical steps are essential for damage control.

results.successDescription: You identified all the critical recovery steps. This quick action can make the difference between a close call and a disaster.
results.partialDescription: In a real incident, missing critical steps could make things worse. Review the steps you missed.

takeaways.clicked_link: Speed matters - disconnecting quickly can prevent malware from spreading or exfiltrating data. Always report even if you're unsure, as IT can assess the real risk.
takeaways.entered_credentials: Password changes must happen immediately from a trusted device. Enable MFA everywhere - it's your best protection even if credentials are stolen.
takeaways.sent_money: The first hour is critical for fund recovery. Banks can sometimes recall wire transfers if notified fast enough. Never delete any evidence.
takeaways.downloaded_file: Don't try to be a hero - well-meaning actions like deleting files or rebooting can destroy forensic evidence or trigger dormant malware.

clicked_link.title: You Clicked a Suspicious Link
clicked_link.description: You realized the link was suspicious after clicking. The page looked like a login portal.

disconnect.title: Disconnect from network
disconnect.description: Turn off WiFi or unplug ethernet to stop any ongoing data transfer

report.title: Report to IT/Security
report.description: Call your IT helpdesk or security team immediately using a known number

scan.title: Run security scan
scan.description: Run antivirus/malware scan to check for drive-by downloads or exploits

document.title: Document what happened
document.description: Note the URL, what you saw, and any actions you took

entered_credentials.title: You Entered Your Password
entered_credentials.description: You entered your username and password on what turned out to be a fake login page.

change_password.title: Change password immediately
change_password.description: Go directly to the real site (type URL manually) and change your password

report.title: Report to IT/Security
report.description: Call IT immediately - they may need to check for account compromise

mfa.title: Enable/review MFA
mfa.description: Ensure multi-factor authentication is enabled; review any new devices

check_accounts.title: Check linked accounts
check_accounts.description: If you reuse passwords (don't!), change them on other sites too

monitor.title: Monitor for suspicious activity
monitor.description: Watch for unusual emails, login alerts, or account changes

sent_money.title: You Transferred Money
sent_money.description: You sent a wire transfer or payment based on what you now realize was a fraudulent request.

bank.title: Contact your bank immediately
bank.description: Call your bank's fraud line RIGHT NOW - time is critical for recovery

report_it.title: Report to IT/Security
report_it.description: They need to know about the breach and may need to alert others

report_fbi.title: File IC3 complaint (FBI)
report_fbi.description: Report to ic3.gov - especially for business email compromise over $10,000

document.title: Preserve all evidence
document.description: Save emails, messages, and transaction records - do not delete anything

notify.title: Notify affected parties
notify.description: If vendor/partner was impersonated, alert them about the fraud

downloaded_file.title: You Downloaded a File
downloaded_file.description: You downloaded and may have opened an attachment or file from a suspicious source.

disconnect.title: Disconnect immediately
disconnect.description: Unplug network cable and disable WiFi to contain potential malware

no_touch.title: Don't try to fix it yourself
no_touch.description: Don't delete files or restart - this may make forensics harder

report.title: Report to IT/Security
report.description: Call IT immediately - they have tools to assess and contain threats

scan.title: Let IT run scans
scan.description: IT may need to run specialized tools or even reimage the device

change_passwords.title: Change passwords (from clean device)
change_passwords.description: After IT clears you, change passwords from a different device
